title: Corporate settlements and donations to Trump's library and ballroom
summary: The settlement amounts and recipients are well documented: ABC $15M and Meta ~$22M of $25M and Paramount $16M (less fees) to the Trump library; X ~$10M (press-reported); YouTube $22M of $24.5M to the ballroom via the Trust for the National Mall. The Oct 2025 White House ballroom donor list does include Coinbase, Ripple, Tether America and both Winklevoss twins, but discloses no amounts. Favorable regulatory outcomes followed for several payers/donors (FCC approval of Skydance-Paramount three weeks after the settlement; SEC dismissals for Coinbase, Gemini, Ripple appeal), but no quid pro quo is documented and the companies deny any link.

sub_claims.statement: ABC/Disney paid $15M to settle Trump's defamation suit, directed to his presidential library.
sub_claims.finding: Signed 13-14 Dec 2024; $15M 'charitable contribution' to a future presidential foundation/museum via escrow at Alejandro Brito's firm, plus $1M legal fees and an editor's note. In 2026 ABC told lawmakers the $15M was still in that escrow.

sub_claims.statement: Meta paid $25M to settle Trump's account-suspension suit, directed to his library.
sub_claims.finding: Reported 29 Jan 2025; ~$22M earmarked for the library, remainder legal fees and co-plaintiffs. Meta also gave $1M to the inaugural fund.

sub_claims.statement: Paramount paid $16M to settle the '60 Minutes' suit, directed to the library.
sub_claims.finding: Announced 1-2 Jul 2025; $16M including plaintiff fees, remainder to the future library; no apology; no payment to Trump personally per Paramount. Trump's claim of ~$20M extra in PSAs is denied by Paramount and unverified.

sub_claims.statement: X settled Trump's suspension suit with a payment.
sub_claims.finding: About $10M per WSJ/CNBC reporting (Feb 2025), confirmed as 'resolved' by Trump lawyer John Kelly; no court filing with the figure found. Democratic lawmakers' letters treat X's payment as going to the (since-dissolved) library fund; recipient not independently confirmed here.

sub_claims.statement: YouTube/Alphabet paid $24.5M, directed to the White House ballroom.
sub_claims.finding: Court filing 29 Sep 2025: $22M (Trump's share) to the Trust for the National Mall for ballroom construction; $2.5M to co-plaintiffs (ACU, Naomi Wolf, others); no admission of liability.

sub_claims.statement: The library money went to Trump-linked entities whose handling is opaque.
sub_claims.finding: Original fund incorporated in Florida 20 Dec 2024, dissolved Sep 2025 for failing to file an annual report; successor Donald J. Trump Presidential Library Foundation Inc. formed May 2025, took title to Miami Dade College land (valued >$67M, deeded for $10) in Feb 2026. Warren/Blumenthal/Stansbury say up to $63M in settlements is unaccounted for. That is an allegation; no foundation response found.

sub_claims.statement: Ballroom donors include crypto firms Coinbase, Ripple, Tether and Gemini's Winklevoss twins.
sub_claims.finding: White House list of ~37 donors released 23-24 Oct 2025 includes Coinbase, Ripple, Tether America and Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss (listed separately), plus Amazon, Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Micron, Lockheed Martin. No amounts disclosed; list admitted incomplete; contract with the Trust for the National Mall allows anonymity. Cost estimate grew $200M to $300M to $400M.

sub_claims.statement: Paramount obtained FCC approval of the Skydance merger after settling.
sub_claims.finding: FCC approved the ~$8B deal 2-1 on 24 Jul 2025, about three weeks after the settlement and 250+ days into review, with Skydance commitments to a CBS ombudsman (2+ years), no DEI programs, and 'viewpoint diversity'. Commissioner Gomez dissented. Timing is documented; causation is not. Paramount says the suit was unrelated.

sub_claims.statement: Other payer/donor companies obtained favorable regulatory outcomes.
sub_claims.finding: SEC dismissed Coinbase case (27 Feb 2025) and closed its Gemini probe (see C23); SEC and Ripple dropped cross-appeals 7 Aug 2025 but the $125M penalty and injunction stand. Public Citizen (Jun 2026) says 19 of 27 identified corporate donors got $338B in federal contracts and 14 face or had suspended enforcement actions (advocacy figures, not independently verified). Audit check on Meta, Google and Disney: the record shows continued or adverse federal action, not favorable treatment. Meta: Trump's FTC took its Instagram/WhatsApp monopoly case to trial. Judge Boasberg ruled for Meta on 2025-11-18, and the FTC said in Jan 2026 that it would appeal. Google: DOJ kept up both cases. Judge Mehta's Sep 2025 search remedies rejected a Chrome divestiture, and DOJ and the states cross-appealed in Feb 2026 seeking it. Judge Brinkema's ad-tech remedy (Sep 2026) declined to order an AdX sale. Those are court rulings, not agency favors. Disney/ABC: FCC Chair Carr opened a DEI probe in Mar 2025, ordered early renewal filings for ABC's eight owned stations in Apr 2026, and opened an equal-time probe of The View. Disney calls these unconstitutional, and no ruling was found as of late July 2026. Tether-specific outcomes were not re-checked.

corrections: The brief groups all settlements with the library; YouTube's $22M went to the White House ballroom via the Trust for the National Mall, not the library.
Headline figures overstate what was earmarked: Meta ~$22M of $25M and YouTube $22M of $24.5M; Paramount's $16M includes plaintiff fees.

No payment went to Trump personally; money went to escrow, a library nonprofit or the Trust for the National Mall. 'Personally linked' rests on Trump's control of the library foundation and ballroom project.
ABC's $15M reportedly remained in escrow at Trump's lawyer's firm as of 2026.
denials_and_context: Paramount says the lawsuit was 'completely separate from, and unrelated to' the Skydance transaction and FCC review, and that it settled to avoid legal costs.
All settlements were made without admission of liability; ABC's was signed before the inauguration, when Trump was president-elect.
The White House says the ballroom is privately funded at no taxpayer cost; donors have not acknowledged any link to regulatory outcomes.
Claims that settlement money is 'missing' come from Democratic lawmakers (Warren, Blumenthal, Stansbury); no foundation response was found.
Public Citizen and Campaign Legal Center analyses are advocacy work; their contract and enforcement tallies were not independently verified.
Research limits: direct fetches mostly failed and the web-search budget ran out before checking 2026 settlements and Tether/Winklevoss regulatory outcomes.

Against the regulatory-favor reading: for three of the biggest payers, Meta, Google/YouTube and Disney/ABC, the administration kept up or escalated enforcement after the settlements (FTC appeal against Meta, Jan 2026; DOJ cross-appeal seeking Chrome divestiture, Feb 2026; FCC license and equal-time probes of ABC, 2026).

leads.title: Missing library settlement money and the dissolved first library fund
leads.why_connected: Up to $63M from ABC, Meta, X and Paramount went to a fund later dissolved; lawmakers say companies cannot account for it and opened a Jul 2026 probe of the Foundation.

leads.title: Miami Dade College land transfer to the Trump library foundation
leads.why_connected: Public land worth more than $67M was deeded for $10 to the Trump-controlled foundation; it is subject to Sunshine-law and constitutional lawsuits.

leads.title: Ballroom donor anonymity contract and government contracts to donors
leads.why_connected: The Trust for the National Mall contract shields donor identities. Public Citizen says 19 of 27 identified corporate donors got $338B in federal contracts and 14 had enforcement actions pending or suspended.

leads.title: Trump library foundation's IRS fast-track during the government shutdown
leads.why_connected: The Miami Herald reported that the foundation got special IRS treatment for its tax-exempt application while projecting about $1B in fundraising.

leads.title: Trump's IRS lawsuit settlement and the $1.776B 'anti-weaponization fund'
leads.why_connected: A 2026 settlement in which Trump dropped a $10B suit against his own government's IRS. DOJ created a fund of about $1.8B, paid from the Treasury Judgment Fund and run by a commission the attorney general appoints. Trump gets an apology and no payment. It is a different kind of 'settlement benefiting Trump-linked interests' from the corporate ones.

changes: Amounts, recipients and the donor list were re-confirmed by AP, Fortune and The Block.

Filled the Meta/Google/Disney gap. All three faced continued or adverse federal action after settling (the FTC is appealing its Meta loss; DOJ is seeking Chrome divestiture on appeal; the FCC is running ABC license and equal-time probes). Added this to sub-claim 9 and to denials_and_context, which cuts against the implied quid pro quo for these payers.

2026 settlements: no new corporate settlement routed to the library or ballroom was found. Added as a lead the May 18, 2026 IRS settlement, which created a $1.776B 'anti-weaponization fund' and paid Trump no money. Verdict unchanged.
